clue.text: Fight clubs replacing bishop with livestock

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means a letter is swapped out for a new one within the word

blocks.note: a battle is a fight
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A fight club has swapped its bishop for a herd of farm animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The C for clubs takes the place of the B for bishop at the front of BATTLE, giving CATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are cows and bulls kept on farms, the commonest kind of livestock.

indicators.note: doing something again means doing it over, so these letters are made up afresh in a new order

blocks.note: an author is a writer
these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A stern writer who keeps wearing a tiara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it is part of the letters to rearrange along with tiara.
explanation.definitionFit: An authoritarian figure demands obedience and enforces rules severely, which is what a strict person does.

clue.text: Extremities of keel held in second little leak

indicators.note: the extremities of something are its two far ends, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
something held in another sits inside it, so one group goes within the other

blocks.note: a trice is a very short moment, like a second
the first and last letters of keel

explanation.surface: The ends of a boat's keel let in a small leak for a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is not the ordinal here but a short moment; 'in a trice' means in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle is a thin, slow flow of liquid, just what a small leak produces.

clue.text: Get lean in order to be graceful

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them properly, so they are sorted into a new sequence

blocks.note: these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to slim down so as to move with grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes someone stylish and refined in movement or appearance, a close synonym for graceful.

indicators.note: something found internally is inside, so the letters lie within the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of chief, all of is and the start of calling

explanation.surface: A head of finance is phoning in from inside the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal relates to government revenue and spending, the matters a budget deals with.

indicators.note: a spin whirls things round, so these letters end up in a different order

blocks.note: these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A car with a flat tyre spinning out of control could kill someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal and lethal both describe something that causes death.

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A Thai restaurant often serves a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs it with Thai food, but the dish is Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese preparation of vinegared rice usually topped or rolled with raw seafood.

clue.text: A thin Corsican travelling out of time

indicators.note: travelling things move about, so these letters shift into another arrangement

blocks.note: all thirteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A slim islander from Corsica is on a journey and running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of time' sounds like running late, but here it means belonging to the wrong era.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anachronistic is misplaced in period, set in the wrong era for its context.

clue.text: New trend – it's loud and harsh

indicators.note: making something new reshapes it, so these letters are formed into a fresh word

blocks.note: these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment that the latest fashion is noisy and jarring.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or sound is grating and forceful, matching both loud and harsh.

clue.text: Lots of water left for marine mammal

blocks.note: a sea is a vast body of water
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Plenty of ocean is left for a sea creature to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a flippered, fish-eating animal that lives along coasts and in the ocean.

blocks.note: first meaning: to arrange a seat or table in advance
second meaning: a printed volume, here one with a soft cover

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like keeping a spare softcover; the two words are separate meanings, one verb and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for securing something in advance and a noun for a bound volume; a paperback is one kind.

blocks.note: first meaning: satisfactory, acceptable
second meaning, read literally: if nothing is on the left side, everything must be on the other side

explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a whimsical literal reading of the phrase; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday synonym for fine or acceptable, and taken word by word means every item lies on the opposite side to left.

blocks.note: to fine someone is to penalise them with a money charge
ST is the address abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: The best way to deal with people is to punish them on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Finest and best are both superlatives meaning of the highest quality.

indicators.note: to harbour something is to shelter it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: 'not on' is an idiom for unacceptable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: It is wrong to cling to a single thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on' is everyday British for that is not acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a belief, concept or thought, so it is a direct synonym for idea.

clue.text: Returning once more with artist to river

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word is written in the opposite direction

blocks.note: again means once more
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A painter comes back once more to the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara is the North American waterway linking Lakes Erie and Ontario, famous for its falls.

clue.text: Swing component put up ahead of rest, we hear

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up lifts it bottom to top, so the word reads backwards
what we hear is a sound, so the word is spelt to match how it is pronounced

blocks.note: a part is a component
ease means rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: Assembling part of a swing set before taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: PART written upwards gives TRAP; then the sound of ease, spelt EZE, completes TRAPEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung from two ropes, a kind of swing used by acrobats.

indicators.note: turned around suggests moving the letters about into a different sequence

blocks.note: these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer a taxi on a tour of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a nation in Southeast Asia, bordering Thailand, Laos and Vietnam.

clue.text: Bachelor and little sister form foundation

blocks.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
sis is a short, familiar form of sister

explanation.surface: An unmarried man and his kid sister set up a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the underlying support or starting point of something, as a foundation is.

blocks.note: D marks drive on an automatic car's gear selector
'tipping down' is British slang for raining hard

explanation.surface: An order to clear a driveway out to the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a dump; in British speech 'it's tipping down' means it is pouring with rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain a container is to let all its liquid flow out, which empties it.

clue.text: Eager for great female singer to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer, especially in opera

explanation.surface: Fans are keen for a star soprano to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid fan is keen and enthusiastic, the same as eager.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: first can mean original, the earliest of its kind

explanation.surface: Nearly the first trees to be planted.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRST loses its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Firs are evergreen conifers with flat needles, a common family of trees.

clue.text: A treat I'm preparing - Italian biscuits

indicators.note: preparing food means mixing ingredients, so these letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker announces a treat in the oven: some Italian cookies.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretti are small almond-flavoured macaroons from Italy, often served with coffee.

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a union is a marriage
S, for south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The whole point of marriage is being together.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside UNION to make UNISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison means acting or sounding as one, in full agreement, which is togetherness.

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up, so these letters are knocked into another order

blocks.note: these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The film star Cagney wrecked a jobs office.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a business that places workers with employers, as an employment bureau does.
